subject: Copywriting
subcategory: The Science of Storytelling in Ads
title: The Peak-End Rule
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Peak-End Rule.

hook.text: You remember a movie by its best moment and its ending. Kahneman proved the peak and the end define the memory.

buildup.text: In experiments, people preferred longer painful procedures if they ended gently.

discovery.text: Ads use this: the emotional climax IS the peak. The brand reveal IS the end. Nail both and the ad is remembered.

twist.text: A forgettable middle doesn't matter if the peak is powerful and the end satisfying. The brain edits the rest out.

climax.text: Budweiser's Super Bowl puppy ads peak at reunion, and end on the logo. The middle is forgotten; the peak endures.

punchline.text: Peak moment plus strong ending. That's how ads get remembered.

quiz.question: What two moments define memory according to the peak-end rule?

details.summary: Daniel Kahneman's peak-end rule states that people judge experiences primarily by their most intense moment (the peak) and their final moment (the end). Ads that nail the emotional climax and the closing beat are remembered more favorably than ads with consistently good but flat engagement.
details.whyItMatters: The peak-end rule tells advertisers exactly where to invest their creative energy. Instead of distributing quality evenly, concentrate resources on creating one transcendent emotional moment and a memorable ending.
takeaways: Memory of an experience is dominated by its peak moment and its ending
A powerful emotional climax can redeem an otherwise mediocre ad
The final beat — tagline, image, or sound — disproportionately shapes brand memory

faq.question: How should the peak-end rule change ad structure?
faq.answer: Design backward from the peak and the ending. Decide what the most intense emotional moment will be and what the final impression should be, then build everything else to set up those two beats. A weak middle is forgivable; a weak peak or ending is not.

faq.question: Can the peak and the end be the same moment?
faq.answer: Yes, and this is often the most powerful structure. Many great ads build to a climactic reveal that is also the closing shot — the moment when the story resolves and the brand appears. This makes both the peak and the end perfect, maximizing memorability.
